mtls.description: Client mTLS identity Keycloak presents to the SE-KIDP on its PAR/token endpoints (A_23183). Enabled only when keystore.secretName is set; also requires authserver.config.oidcFlowEnabled: true (otherwise the plugin never loads the keystore and rendering fails). Total worst-case = replicaCount × maxSize; this (+ ~25 CNPG/superuser reserve) must stay ≤ cloudnativePg.parameters.maxConnections, otherwise the chart fails the render (SQLSTATE 53300 / DB crash under load). Values above authserver.httpPool.maxThreads are wasteful. Default is minimal; scale-out stages raise it in their overlay together with maxConnections and cloudnativePg.resources.

locations.description: DEPRECATED — use `proxyLocations`; this raw form is scheduled for removal, and MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `proxyLocations` (the render fails hard when both are set). Additional Nginx location blocks injected into the generated config. NOTE: `proxy_headers.conf` is included at server level, but nginx proxy_set_header inheritance is non-additive — any location declaring its own `proxy_set_header` must repeat `include proxy_headers.conf;`, otherwise `pep on;` locations fail with HTTP 500 (ProxyHeadersMissing).

proxyLocations.description: Structured proxied resource-server paths. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with the deprecated raw `locations` (the render fails hard when both are set). Each entry generates an http-level upstream block with connection keepalive plus an exact + trailing-slash location pair that always includes proxy_headers.conf. Entries with websocket: true also feed the dedicated ingress WebSocket minion.

path.description: Public path; must start with / and must not end with / (the exact + prefix location pair is generated).

upstream.description: scheme://host[:port] of the resource server — no path component (use upstreamPath).

upstreamPath.description: URI prefix on the upstream the location maps to. Default: / (strips the public path prefix).

websocket.description: Emit WebSocket upgrade handling and route this path via the dedicated ingress ws minion.

bypassAsl.description: satisfy all; allow all; — makes the path publicly reachable WITHOUT the ASL protocol. Ensure your resource server's spec permits this.

keepalive.description: Idle upstream connections cached per nginx worker. Default: 32.

extraConfig.description: Raw nginx directives appended inside both generated location blocks (tpl-rendered).

pepIssuer.description: OIDC issuer (iss) of the authorization server used for access token validation. This is used for token validation as well as for retvrieving the JWKS and similar things.

quarter: within the current quarter (see gemSpec_ZETA — A_26477)
duration string: fixed validity period, since iat + optional unit (d,h,m,s); defaults to s if no unit given.

Mutually exclusive with provisioningContainerCaSecretRef (SecretRef takes precedence if both are set). The certificate is mounted as /var/registry-ca/ca.crt in each init container and sets PROVISIONING_CONTAINER_REGISTRY_CA_FILE accordingly.

key.description: Key within the ConfigMap that holds the PEM certificate data.

telemetry-gateway.description: OpenTelemetry Collector deployment that aggregates and exports telemetry data. Configured via the opentelemetry-collector subchart.

telemetryGatewayHost.description: Sets the hostname under which the telemetry-gateway is reached (PEP OTLP traces + syslog, OPA OTLP, authserver OTLP). Empty uses the default bundled collector name (telemetry-gateway.fullnameOverride, else "<release>-telemetry-gateway"). Set to the fully-qualified hostname of the telemetry-gateway when the bare service name does not resolve (cluster DNS not applying the pod search path, cross-namespace, or a non-default cluster domain), e.g. "zeta-guard-telemetry-gateway.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local". As a Helm value it survives upgrades — no ConfigMap hand-editing (forbidden in production); same pattern as authserver.provider.smcB.opaBaseUrl. This changes ONLY the address, never the destination: telemetry must always go to the telemetry-gateway, whose redaction and ti_sim/ti_siem filters are not bypassable — attach your own backend as an exporter inside the gateway's dienst_hersteller pipelines. Hostname only — ports are fixed. Requires matching egress when the gateway runs outside this chart.

telemetryGatewayEnabled.description: Include the telemetry gateway in the Helm release. SHOULD BE true FOR PRODUCTION.

telemetryGatewaySendingQueuePVCResources.description: Sizes the PersistentVolumeClaim backing the sending queue

telemetryGatewaySendingQueuePVCAccessMod.description: Access modes of the PersistentVolumeClaim backing the sending queue. ReadWriteOnce fits the single-replica deployment on block storage; use ReadWriteMany on a shared filesystem (Azure Files, CephFS, NFS) when the storage system offers nothing else. ReadWriteMany also lifts the single-writer constraint that telemetry-gateway.rollout works around with maxSurge: 0.

telemetryGatewaySendingQueuePVCStorageCl.description: StorageClass of the PersistentVolumeClaim backing the sending queue. Empty omits the field, so the cluster's default StorageClass applies. Set it when that default cannot be attached by your nodes (the gateway then hangs in ContainerCreating with FailedAttachVolume) or cannot serve the requested access modes. A PVC spec is immutable: a claim already created with the wrong class has to be deleted once before the next upgrade recreates it.

enabled.description: Enable OPA bundle mode. When false, inline policyRego is used.

serviceName.description: Logical service name used in OPA config to identify the bundle source.

url.description: Base URL of the OCI/Docker registry serving bundles.

resource.description: Fully qualified bundle resource path including registry host.

min_delay_seconds.description: Minimum polling delay in seconds between bundle download attempts.

max_delay_seconds.description: Maximum polling delay in seconds between bundle download attempts.

enabled.description: Enable cryptographic signature verification for downloaded bundles. THIS SHOULD BE true IN PRODUCTION!

keyId.description: Key ID that must match the signing key embedded in the bundle. You can usually leave this alone and rely on the default.

algorithm.description: Signature algorithm used to verify the bundle. You can usually leave this alone and rely on the default.

publicKey.description: PEM-encoded public key for bundle signature verification. DO NOT TOUCH FOR PRODUCTION!

scope.description: Must match the scope embedded in the bundle signature. Omit if the bundle was signed without a scope.

secretRef.description: Reference to a Kubernetes Secret holding registry bearer credentials.

name.description: Name of the Secret in the release namespace. Empty string disables credential injection (e.g. in WIF mode).

bundleHealthCheck.description: Require an activated bundle for readiness. When true and bundle.enabled=true, the readiness probe uses /health?bundles=true, so a failed bundle download makes the pod NotReady instead of failing silently. The liveness probe stays on /health.

containerSecurityContext.description: Kubernetes SecurityContext applied to the trust-anchor provisioning processor init container in OPA deployments. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/

resources.description: CPU and memory resource requests/limits for the provisioning processor in OPA deployments.

containerSecurityContext.description: Kubernetes SecurityContext applied to the opa container. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/

cronjobSecurityContext.description: Kubernetes SecurityContext applied to the OPA-related CronJob containers (e.g. token renewer). See https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/

serviceAccountName.description: Kubernetes ServiceAccount name for OPA pods. Required for Workload Identity Federation.

image.description: Container image overrides for opa deployments.

imagePullPolicy.description: Kubernetes image pull policy for the OPA container.

imagePullSecrets.description: Image pull secrets for the OPA container.

resources.description: CPU and memory resource requests/limits for the OPA container.

workloadIdentityFederation.description: Workload Identity Federation for accessing Google Artifact Registry without static credentials.

enabled.description: Enable Workload Identity Federation for OPA bundle downloads from GAR.

sts.description: Google Security Token Service (STS) configuration. STS/IAM endpoints and scope are fixed in the token-renewer CronJob; the audience is derived from gematik.workloadIdentityFederation.*.

sa.description: Google service account email to impersonate.

tokenRenewer.description: CronJob that periodically refreshes the WIF access token.

enabled.description: Enable the token renewer CronJob.

schedule.description: Cron schedule expression for token renewal.

backoffLimit.description: Number of retries for failed token renewal Jobs.

rolloutRestart.description: CronJob that periodically restarts the opa (and, if enabled, opa-simulation) Deployment via `kubectl rollout restart`.

enabled.description: Enable the rollout-restart CronJob. Disabled by default.

serviceAccountName.description: Externally pre-provisioned ServiceAccount to run the CronJob as. Leave empty (default) to let the chart create its own ServiceAccount and minimal RBAC (get/patch on the opa/opa-simulation Deployments only).

schedule.description: Cron schedule expression for the rollout restart.

backoffLimit.description: Number of retries for failed rollout-restart Jobs.

resources.description: CPU and memory resource requests/limits for the rollout-restart CronJob container.

simulation.description: OPA simulation instance for shadow policy evaluation.

enabled.description: Deploy a second OPA instance that evaluates policies in shadow mode.

bundle.description: Bundle configuration specific to the simulation OPA instance.

resource.description: Bundle resource path for the simulation instance.

verification.description: Optional signature verification override for the simulation bundle. If empty, opa.bundle.verification applies.

enabled.description: Enable cryptographic signature verification for downloaded bundles. THIS SHOULD BE true IN PRODUCTION!

keyId.description: Key ID that must match the signing key embedded in the bundle. You can usually leave this alone and rely on the default.

algorithm.description: Signature algorithm used to verify the bundle. You can usually leave this alone and rely on the default.

scope.description: Must match the scope embedded in the bundle signature. Omit if the bundle was signed without a scope.

podLabels.description: Additional labels to add to the OPA pod.

podAnnotations.description: Additional Kubernetes annotations for the OPA pod.

affinity.description: Kubernetes affinity rules for OPA pod scheduling.

tolerations.description: Kubernetes tolerations for OPA pod scheduling.

notificationService.description: Bundled ZETA Notification Service (push notification facade for TI 2.0 services), reachable through the PEP under the /push/v1 path prefix.

enabled.description: Deploy the notification-service component and wire its PEP location block.

serviceAccountName.description: Kubernetes ServiceAccount name for notification-service pods.

image.description: Shared container image overrides for both notification-service variants (registry/repository/digest). The per-variant tag defaults to "<image.tag>-<variant>" unless overridden under rs/fdv.

rs.description: RS-facing variant overrides. Deployed as notification-service-rs (internal ClusterIP; reached in-cluster by resource servers, not via the PEP).

tag.description: Full image tag for the rs variant. Empty -> "<image.tag>-rs".

digest.description: Optional image digest override for the rs variant.

fdv.description: FdV-facing variant overrides. Deployed as notification-service-fdv (the PEP proxies /push/v1/* here).

tag.description: Full image tag for the fdv variant. Empty -> "<image.tag>-fdv".

digest.description: Optional image digest override for the fdv variant.

db.description: Database persistence for the notification-service (both variants share one database). cloudnative mode is PostgreSQL (CNPG); external mode supports the kinds listed under db.kind.

mode.description: cloudnative -> provision a dedicated CNPG Cluster (cloudnativePg); external -> use an out-of-band database via jdbcUrl/secretName.

kind.description: Database kind, passed as NOTIFICATION_DATASOURCE_DB_KIND (notification.datasource.db-kind, no application-side default). cloudnative mode (CNPG) requires postgresql; the template fails the render otherwise.

jdbcUrl.description: JDBC URL (QUARKUS_DATASOURCE_JDBC_URL). Empty in cloudnative mode -> derived as "jdbc:postgresql://<clusterName>-rw:5432/notification" (the CNPG -rw service, database "notification"). Set explicitly for an external DB.

secretName.description: Secret holding datasource username/password (keys: username, password). Empty in cloudnative mode -> derived as "<clusterName>-app" (the CNPG-generated secret). Set explicitly for an external DB.

clusterName.description: Name of the CNPG Cluster provisioned in cloudnative mode. Single source of truth: the Cluster, its -rw/-app resources, the egress NetworkPolicy and istio PeerAuthentication selectors, and the derived jdbcUrl/secretName/waitForDb.host all follow this name.

waitForDb.description: Init container that blocks each notification-service pod until Postgres accepts TCP connections (avoids crash-looping on Flyway's startup connection). Mirrors the push-gateway wait-for-dependencies pattern.

enabled.description: Add the wait-for-db init container to both notification-service variants.

image.description: Image providing `nc` for the TCP probe (default: the pinned busybox image the push-gateway chart uses).

cloudnativePg.description: CNPG Cluster settings, used only when mode=cloudnative. Plain Postgres (no pg_cron).

allOf.$comment: External DB has no CNPG cluster to derive from, so jdbcUrl/secretName must be set explicitly; leaving them empty would silently target the in-cluster <clusterName>-rw/-app resources that only exist in cloudnative mode.

imagePullPolicy.description: Kubernetes image pull policy for the notification-service container.

imagePullSecrets.description: Image pull secrets for the notification-service container.

containerSecurityContext.description: Kubernetes SecurityContext applied to the notification-service container. See https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/security-context/

env.description: Application configuration for notification-service, mapped to container env vars.

pushGatewayAllowedBaseUrls.description: Allowlist of Push Gateway base URLs, joined with "," into PUSH_GATEWAY_ALLOWED_BASE_URLS. The service has no default for this property, so an empty list is expected to fail config validation at startup — set at least one URL when enabling this component.

channelsAllowed.description: Comma-separated list of allowed notification channels (NOTIFICATION_CHANNELS_ALLOWED). The service has no default for this property either — set at least one channel name when enabling this component.

persistenceSealingEnabled.description: Enable HSM-backed at-rest sealing of stored notification data (NOTIFICATION_PERSISTENCE_SEALING_ENABLED).

pushGateway.description: Configuration for the notification-service's outbound HTTPS calls to the (external) Push Gateway.

trustedCAs.description: Additional CA(s) trusted for the NS's outbound HTTPS calls to the Push Gateway, in addition to the system default anchors (the app merges them). List the CA here when the Push Gateway is reached via an ingress whose CA the default trust store does not know (self-signed local issuer, Let's Encrypt staging). Each cert is mounted at /certs/push-gateway/ca-<i>.pem and passed via PUSH_GATEWAY_TRUSTED_CA_PATHS (only emitted when non-empty). Each entry references an existing Secret+key (secretName + secretKey) or supplies an inline PEM (cert).

mtls.description: Client certificate identity the NS presents to the Push Gateway for outbound mTLS. Enabled only when BOTH clientCert.secretName and clientKey.secretName are set (the service requires cert and key together; setting exactly one fails rendering). Cert and key are mounted at /certs/push-gateway-client/tls.crt and /certs/push-gateway-client/tls.key and passed via PUSH_GATEWAY_MTLS_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH / PUSH_GATEWAY_MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_PATH.

clientCert.description: Existing Secret holding the PEM client certificate chain (e.g. a kubernetes.io/tls Secret or a cert-manager Certificate).

secretName.description: Name of an existing Secret holding the PEM client certificate chain. Empty disables mTLS.

secretKey.description: Key within the referenced Secret that holds the PEM client certificate chain.

clientKey.description: Existing Secret holding the PEM private key. May be the same Secret as clientCert or a different one.

secretName.description: Name of an existing Secret holding the PEM private key. Empty disables mTLS.

secretKey.description: Key within the referenced Secret that holds the PEM private key.

keyPassword.description: Optional password for an encrypted private key (PUSH_GATEWAY_MTLS_CLIENT_KEY_PASSWORD). Secret reference only; omit for unencrypted keys. Only emitted when secretName is set.

secretName.description: Name of an existing Secret holding the private key password.

secretKey.description: Key within the referenced Secret that holds the private key password. Required when secretName is set.

accessLog.description: Quarkus built-in HTTP access log (quarkus.http.access-log.*), mapped to QUARKUS_HTTP_ACCESS_LOG_* container env vars. Useful for tracing requests reaching the notification-service, e.g. confirming the PEP-forwarded ZETA-User-Info header.

enabled.description: Enable the Quarkus HTTP access log (QUARKUS_HTTP_ACCESS_LOG_ENABLED). Off by default.

pattern.description: Access log pattern (QUARKUS_HTTP_ACCESS_LOG_PATTERN). Empty uses the Quarkus default ("common"). Use %{i,Header-Name} to capture an incoming request header, e.g. %h "%r" %s %b user-info="%{i,ZETA-User-Info}".

resources.description: CPU and memory resource requests/limits for the notification-service container.

podAnnotations.description: Additional Kubernetes annotations for the notification-service pod.

podLabels.description: Additional Kubernetes labels for the notification-service pod.

affinity.description: Kubernetes affinity rules for the notification-service pod.

tolerations.description: Kubernetes tolerations for the notification-service pod.

historyEnabled.description: A_29974: single knob for the optional history feature — drives the NS's NOTIFICATION_HISTORY_ENABLED env var, the discovery doc's scopes_supported, and (via terraform notification_history_enabled, kept in sync) the Keycloak scope.

wellKnownResourceSuffix.description: RFC 9728 resource identifier for the NS (source of truth; NS analog of pepproxy.wellKnownResourceSuffix). Combined with pepproxy.wellKnownBase to form the aud; the well-known location, `resource` field, pep_require_aud, and ConfigMap key/path all derive from it. Decoupled from the /push/v1 API prefix. Must be a single leading-slash segment.

ingressMasterAnnotations.description: Extra annotations added to the master Ingress resource.

ingressMinionAnnotations.description: Extra annotations added to minion (path-based) Ingress resources.

routeViaTigerProxy.description: When true, the Ingress routes traffic through the tiger-proxy service instead of directly exposing internal services. DO NOT USE IN PRODUCTION

ingressClassName.description: IngressClass used by generated Ingress resources. Must match the NIC class name if the bundled NIC is enabled.

issuer.description: cert-manager namespace-scoped Issuer name used for TLS certificates on Ingress resources. Takes precedence over clusterIssuer when set.

clusterIssuer.description: cert-manager ClusterIssuer name used for TLS certificates on Ingress resources. If an `issuer` is defined, it takes precedence over `clusterIssuer`.

certificateAdoption.description: One-shot post-install/post-upgrade hook Job that adopts pre-existing ingress-shim-created Certificates into the helm release. Only rendered while such a foreign Certificate exists.

image.description: Image for the adoption Job; needs kubectl and bash.

openshiftIngress.description: OpenShift Ingress Route-Controller with TLS. Creates edge-terminated routes with TLS redirect via OpenShift's Ingress-to-Route controller. nginxIngressEnabled should be false

enabled.description: When true, add TLS configuration to Ingress resources for OpenShift's route controller.

certName.description: Name of the TLS Secret referenced in Ingress TLS blocks.

nginxIngressEnabled.description: When true, render F5-NIC-specific annotations on the Ingresses (mergeable-ingress-type, websocket-services, lb-method, ...). Does not install the NIC; the bundled subchart is gated by nginx-ingress.enabled.

nginxIngressHsm.description: When true, disable spec.tls of the master ingress to enable custom TLS configuration via ingressMasterAnnotations."nginx.org/server-snippets", as required for ossl_hsm support.

nginxIngressLbMethod.description: When true, add the cookie-based sticky-session lb-method (hash $zeta_route consistent) on the minion ingress. Requires the NIC to provide the $zeta_route http-snippets; disable for external NICs without them.

nginx-ingress.description: Configuration passed to the bundled nginx-ingress subchart.

enabled.description: When true, install the bundled F5 NIC subchart. Set false on stages where the NIC is installed out-of-band (e.g. openshift, qs). Annotation rendering is controlled separately by nginxIngressEnabled.

name.description: Name of the IngressClass resource to be monitored by the ingress controller. Relevant for namespace isolation.

pod.description: Settings applied to the NIC controller pod template.

annotations.description: Annotations on the NIC controller pod template. Changing any value triggers a rolling restart.

entries.description: Key-value map of NGINX configuration directives.

http-snippets.description: Raw http-level NGINX directives. Includes more_clear_input_headers, which strips client-supplied forwarding and client-address headers (Forwarded, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, vendor/CDN variants, ...) so that only this ingress determines the client address. The authorization server derives the access token's client-address claim from these headers, and the PEP enforces that claim against every request, so a client able to inject one can choose its own address. If you REMOVE a header from that list because you need to trust a reverse proxy in front of this ingress, you are responsible for stripping the incoming forwarding headers *at that proxy* - otherwise clients can spoof their address again.

ssl-ecdh-curve.description: Allowed ECDH curves for TLS key exchange.

ssl-session-tickets.description: Enable or disable TLS session tickets.

ssl-prefer-server-ciphers.description: Prefer server cipher order over client preference.

enableCustomResources.description: Install ingress controller's custom resource definitions (VirtualServer, etc.). Disable if only using standard Ingress. Not required for ZETA.

service.description: Kubernetes Service configuration for the ingress controller.

type.description: Service type for the ingress controller.

externalTrafficPolicy.description: External traffic policy for the ingress controller Service.

devMode.description: When true, inject a changing annotation on each helm upgrade to force pod rollouts even if the image tag is unchanged. May/will lead to unneccesary restarts.

registry_name.description: Registry path segment appended after global.registry_host for zeta-guard images.

networkPolicy.description: Egress NetworkPolicy configuration (A_27864-01). When enabled, each ZETA Guard pod receives an egress NetworkPolicy restricting outbound traffic to the explicitly listed IP blocks. Internal cluster traffic (DNS, pod-to-pod) is always allowed.

enabled.description: Enable egress NetworkPolicies for all ZETA Guard pods.

dns.description: DNS egress peer shared by all egress NetworkPolicies. Defaults to the upstream kube-dns service. For OpenShift, set the openshift-dns selector and port 5353 (OVN-Kubernetes evaluates egress post-DNAT, so the pod port is 5353). Set 'to' for a fully custom peer list that overrides the selectors.

namespaceSelector.description: Namespace selector for the DNS peer. Ignored when 'to' is set.

matchLabels.description: Labels identifying the namespace that hosts the DNS pods.

podSelector.description: Pod selector for the DNS peer. Ignored when 'to' is set.

ports.description: Ports allowed to the DNS peer. Use 5353 on OpenShift (post-DNAT pod port).

to.description: Raw NetworkPolicyPeer list rendered verbatim as the DNS egress peers. When non-empty, overrides namespaceSelector/podSelector. Use to express selectors this schema does not model.

egress.description: Egress rule sets, one per external destination category.

artifactRegistry.description: A_27864-01 — ZETA Artifact Registry at gematik (image pulls, OPA bundles).

ocspCabForum.description: A_27864-01 — OCSP/CRL for TLS TSPs per CAB Forum.

ocspTiPki.description: A_27864-01 — OCSP Responder TSP Komponenten PKI der TI.

pip.description: PIP — source of OPA policy bundles.

mock.description: Allow egress to the local popp-mock pod via podSelector (app=popp-mock) on targetPort 8080. For use with the popp-mocks subchart in local KIND stages only.

providerInternal.description: Provider specific (German anbieterspezifisch) egress rules for resource servers, telemetry systems, and cluster-local pods.

allowAll.description: When true, all egress is permitted without IP filtering (overrides all other providerInternal rules). Use only in controlled environments.

resourceServers.description: IP blocks for provider-internal resource servers (e.g. JWK fetch endpoint via ingress). Use HOST_IP/32 for local KIND stages.

telemetrySystems.description: IP blocks for provider-internal telemetry systems.

podSelectors.description: Allow egress to cluster-local pods by label selector (post-DNAT, kindnet pattern). Use for test-only cluster-local backends such as testfachdienst in local KIND stages.

matchLabels.description: Label selector that identifies the target pods.

port.description: Target port (post-DNAT) on the destination pod. Must be the container port, not the Service port.

TrustedCaList.description: List of additional trusted CA certificates. Each entry references an existing Secret+key (secretName + secretKey) OR supplies an inline PEM (cert); exactly one of the two forms must be set per entry.

secretName.description: Name of an existing Secret holding one PEM-encoded CA certificate.

secretKey.description: Key within the referenced Secret that holds the PEM-encoded CA certificate.

cert.description: Inline PEM-encoded CA certificate; the chart materializes it into a chart-managed Secret.

ZetaImage.description: Container image reference with optional registry override and digest pinning.

registry.description: Registry override for this specific image.

K8sImagePullSecrets.description: List of Kubernetes image pull secret references.

name.description: Name of the referenced Kubernetes resource.

K8sResourceRequirements.description: Compute resources required by this container.

limits.description: Maximum compute resources the container may consume.

requests.description: Minimum compute resources guaranteed to the container.

K8sPodSecurityContext.description: Pod-level security context. Applied to all containers in the pod.

create.description: Create a dedicated ServiceAccount for this workload.

name.description: Name of the ServiceAccount to use.

initialDelaySeconds.description: Number of seconds after the container has started before the probe is initiated.

periodSeconds.description: How often (in seconds) to perform the probe.

failureThreshold.description: Number of consecutive failures before the probe is considered failed.

timeoutSeconds.description: Number of seconds after which the probe times out.

successThreshold.description: Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed.

K8sPodDisruptionBudget.description: PodDisruptionBudget configuration. Either minAvailable or maxUnavailable can be set, but not both.

enabled.description: Create a PodDisruptionBudget for this workload.

minAvailable.description: Minimum number/percentage of pods that must remain available.

maxUnavailable.description: Maximum number/percentage of pods that can be unavailable.

NetPolIpBlockList.description: List of CIDR blocks for a NetworkPolicy egress rule.

items.description: A CIDR block in prefix/length notation.

NetPolIpBlockRule.description: Egress rule containing a list of CIDR blocks for one external destination category.
